purpose: This medication is used to treat high blood pressure and fluid buildup (swelling) in the body. It helps your body get rid of extra water and salt through your urine. By reducing fluid and lowering blood pressure, it helps protect your heart, kidneys, and blood vessels.
how_it_works: This medicine is actually two water pills combined into one. Hydrochlorothiazide tells your kidneys to flush out extra salt and water from your body. Triamterene is added to help your body hold onto potassium, which the first medicine can sometimes wash away — so they work together as a team.
common_side_effects: You may need to urinate more often, especially when you first start taking it. Other common effects include dizziness (especially when standing up quickly), mild nausea, headache, or feeling tired. Some people notice increased sensitivity to sunlight, so wearing sunscreen is a good idea.
warnings: This medication can affect your potassium levels — too high or too low potassium can cause serious heart problems. Avoid taking extra potassium supplements or salt substitutes unless your doctor says it is okay. Tell your doctor right away if you notice muscle weakness, irregular heartbeat, or very little urination. People with kidney problems, liver disease, or diabetes should use this medicine with extra caution. Do not stop taking it without talking to your doctor first.
typical_dosing: The usual dose is one capsule or tablet taken once or twice a day, often in the morning to avoid waking up at night to use the bathroom. Always take it exactly as your doctor prescribes. Taking it with food or milk can help reduce stomach upset.
